verdict.rationale: The only on-topic evidence is the Server Administration Guide listing brute-force protection events such as 'User disabled by permanent lockout' and 'temporary lockout', plus a note that users can view their account history. Together these suggest Keycloak records some authentication-related security events, but only glancingly; metrics collection is a different capability and earns no credit. missing for 10: documented admin-activity event capture, comprehensive authentication event logging, tamper-evidence or integrity protection of logs, streaming or export to a SIEM (event listeners, syslog or HTTP sinks), and independent or hands-on corroboration.
